analysis: Nadir orchard tiles are rotation- and flip-symmetric, so I enable the full flip set and substantial rotation (round peaches suffer minimal axis-aligned box distortion under rotation). The class-discriminative signal is the orange/yellow hue of peach fragments against green foliage, so I keep hue jitter tight while allowing generous saturation/brightness variation to model outdoor illumination changes. Because 52% of objects are already COCO-small and mosaic itself downsizes sources, I moderate scale-down zoom, keep mosaic at full strength (it densifies sparse scenes and mimics tile-edge truncation), and disable label-blending/warping augmentations (mixup, cutmix, shear, perspective, bgr) that corrupt tiny color cues or produce off-distribution geometry. This gives an interpretable, domain-grounded anchor whose individual knobs can be perturbed deliberately in later trials.
hsv_h_just: Hue is the primary cue separating orange/yellow peaches from green canopy; large hue shifts could turn peaches green or foliage orange, destroying the class signal. A small jitter near the default handles minor camera/white-balance variation without corrupting the discriminative channel.
hsv_s_just: Outdoor drone imagery varies in saturation with sun angle, haze, and exposure, and saturation jitter preserves hue ordering, so peaches stay 'orange-ish'. A moderately strong value near the default gives illumination robustness that a small dataset needs.
hsv_v_just: Brightness varies strongly across drone flights (shadows under canopy vs. sunlit ground) and value jitter is the most realistic photometric variation; occluded peaches in shadow are common, so I go slightly above default.
degrees_just: Nadir imagery has no canonical orientation, so rotation produces perfectly in-distribution images; peaches are round, so rotating them barely inflates their axis-aligned boxes. I use the maximum allowed range to exploit this true invariance, which combined with flips covers most of the rotation group.
translate_just: Translation reproduces the tile-edge truncation already present in 21% of boxes and shifts sparse objects across the canvas; a modest value adds this realistic variation without pushing most single-peach tiles' only object out of frame.
scale_just: Half the peaches are already COCO-small (p5 = 12 px at training resolution), and mosaic further downsizes sources, so aggressive scale-down risks pushing objects below detectability; some zoom variation is still realistic (flight-altitude drift). I reduce below the 0.5 default to protect small-object recall.
shear_just: Shear produces parallelogram distortions that never occur in nadir orthomosaic tiles and distorts the tight boxes of small round fruit; it is off-distribution, so I disable it.
perspective_just: Perspective warp models oblique viewing angles absent from straight-down 15 m captures; the warp also corrupts tiny bounding boxes disproportionately, so I disable it.
flipud_just: Vertical flips are exactly in-distribution for nadir imagery with no canonical up direction; a 0.5 probability doubles effective geometric diversity at zero label cost.
fliplr_just: Horizontal flips are likewise a true invariance of the nadir scene; keep the standard 0.5 probability.
bgr_just: Channel swapping turns orange peaches blue — a categorical destruction of the single most discriminative cue in this task. Disable entirely.
mosaic_just: Mosaic is the strongest regularizer available for a 1,781-image dataset and a nano model: it densifies sparse scenes (median 1 instance/tile), diversifies context (canopy vs. ground peaches in one canvas), and its edge-cutting mimics the tiling truncation seen at validation. The downsizing cost to small objects is partially offset by the reduced scale setting and STAL's small-object assignment, so I keep it at full probability.
mixup_just: Alpha-blending two images washes out the faint color fragments that are the only evidence for occluded small peaches and creates ghost labels; harmful for tiny-object color-cue detection, so disable.
cutmix_just: Pasted rectangles can cover or bisect tiny peaches, creating label noise disproportionate to any regularization gain in a sparse single-class scene; disable for the baseline.
copy_paste_just: With box-only labels, copy-paste has limited or no effect in Ultralytics and any box-level paste would carry rectangular background patches that create artifacts around tiny objects; disable.
close_mosaic_just: Fine-tuning the final epochs on full-resolution, unfragmented tiles lets the model calibrate to the true validation object-size distribution after mosaic's downsizing pressure; the default 10 epochs gives a meaningful mosaic-free phase even if early stopping trims a few epochs.
